info.name: notify-service
info.description:
notify: send notifications over SMS, Email, WhatsApp and Push.

Run the requests in this order the first time:
  1. Notification Configs > Create config - welcome-email
  2. Providers > List providers   (confirm a provider loaded)
  3. Provider Mappings > Create mapping - EMAIL to gmail
  4. Notify > Send notification (Email only)

baseUrl: use http://localhost:8080 locally (no context path). In a deployment the service runs under /notify, so use https://<host>/notify.

Every request takes X-Tenant-ID as a header; it is never read from the body.

See README.md for the full guide, including how to write a provider.

item.name: Provider Mappings
item.description: Which vendor a channel uses, per tenant. providers is an ordered fallback chain. An optional country routes on the recipient's countryCode; a mapping without one is the catch-all. Creating a mapping that names a provider which is not loaded is rejected with 400.

request.description: The catch-all EMAIL mapping (no country). One per tenant -- the unique index covers (tenant, channel) where country is null.

A country-specific EMAIL mapping, which is why it does not collide with the catch-all above. The providers array is ordered: had a second EMAIL provider been loaded it would be tried when the first fails. Only gmail is loaded here, so the list has one entry.
Country-specific SMS. Preferred over the catch-all for a recipient whose countryCode is IN.
Used for any country with no specific mapping. Names smscountry because that is what is actually loaded -- a provider absent from GET /v3/providers is rejected with 400.
All mappings for the tenant.

item.name: Send to one channel only (others SKIPPED)

request.description: Same otp-login config, but only an email address is supplied. SMS, WHATSAPP and PUSH come back SKIPPED with "No <address> on recipient" -- not FAILED -- and no notification_attempt row is written for them. This is how you send on some of a template's channels and not others: supply only the addresses you want used.

exec: // EMAIL was attempted -- whether the vendor accepted it depends on the address, so this
// asserts it was not skipped rather than that it was delivered.
// The point: an address the caller did not supply is a choice, not a failure.
pm.test('SMS names the missing address', () => pm.expect(by.SMS.reason).to.include('phone number'));

item.description: Read-only view of the jars that loaded. Providers are not created through the API -- they appear because their jar is in NOTIFY_PLUGINS_DIR and their credentials are set. A provider missing from this list has credentials missing; the startup log names the variable.

Sets isActive true, deliberately. The provider registry lives in the SHARED schema, not a tenant's -- it describes which jars this pod loaded -- so flipping a provider off here disables it for every tenant on the cluster, and a collection run would leave it that way. If you want to test deactivation, do it by hand and turn it back on.

item.name: Tenant provisioning
item.description:
Proves tenant-migration is actually in effect, not just configured. Uses a tenant name generated per run, so it is repeatable: the first call must FAIL because that tenant has no schema, and the same call must succeed once it does.

If the first call returned data instead of erroring, requests would be reaching the shared schema and separation would not be working. Only relevant when TENANT_MIGRATION_ENABLED=true.

exec: // A name unique to this run, so the negative control is still negative on a re-run.
// The shared schema holds configs for other tenants. If separation is working this tenant
// cannot see them -- its own schema does not exist yet, so the query has no table to read.
pm.test('did NOT return another tenant\'s configs', () => {

No body -- the tenant comes from the header. 200 done, 409 migration disabled, 400 unusable tenant id (blank, over 63 chars, lowercase 'public', or a pg_ prefix). Exempt from the tenant filter, because the schema it creates does not exist yet.
